title: Part Two, Chapter 9: The Dark House and the House of Knives

verses.t: There they entered the dark house, and then they went to give them their torch of pine, which was shining when it arrived, and to each of them a cigar as well, by the messengers of Hun-came; and they said to them, "Here is your torch and these cigars, say the lords; in the morning you are to give them back, though they have burned all night." This is what the messengers said when they arrived. "Very well," they said, and they did not light the torch, but put something else that was red in place of the torch, which was the tail feathers of a macaw; and to those who stood guard, keeping watch, it looked like a burning torch. And on the cigars they put fireflies; and all night the guards thought them beaten, and said, "They are already caught." And the torch was not used up, nor the cigars either; they had burned none of them. And then they went to give back the torch and the cigars to the lords, who said, "What is this? Where have these come from? Who begot them and who bore them? Truly our hearts are burning, for what they are doing is not good. Strange are their faces, and strange are their ways." This is what they said among themselves. And then all the lords sent to call them: "Come, let us play ball, young men." And Hun-came and Vucub-came asked them, "Where have you come from? Tell us, young men." And they said, "We do not know where we come from," and they did not tell. "Very well," said those of the underworld to them. "Come, let us play ball, young men. Where shall we put this ball of ours, of rubber?" said those of the underworld. "In no way; you will throw yours," said the young men. And those of the underworld said, "It cannot be any but ours." "Very well," said the young men. "Come, let it be this little worm called Chil," said those of the underworld. "Not that," said the boys, "but the head of the puma." "Not that," said those of the underworld. "Very well," said Hun-ahpu. And then those of the underworld threw the ball, and it went straight to Hun-ahpu's yoke; and when those of the underworld saw the sharp blow as the ball left the bat, it went bounding over the ground. "What is this?" said Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque. "Do you only want our death? Did you not send to call us? Did not your messengers come? Poor us! We shall go away again," said the young men to them. For this is what they wanted for the young men, that they should die at once in the ball game; but they were not beaten. Not so those of the underworld, who were beaten again by the boys. And they said to them, "Let us play ball; we shall throw yours," it was said to the young men. And they said, "Very well," and then they threw their rubber ball; and then the ball game ended. And those of the underworld said, "What shall we do to beat them?" And they said to the young men, "You will bring us four gourds of flowers." "Very well," said the young men. "And what flowers do you want?" said the young men to those of the underworld. "We want," they said, "Cacamuchih and Saquimuchih, Zanamuchit and also Carinimac." "Very well," said the young men. And then they went down to a house where there was nothing but knives of obsidian (chay), all alike and strong; and there were many of these blades. And the hearts of those of the underworld were glad when they put them among the knives, so that the two young men might be beaten; and those of the underworld were glad when they thought they had already beaten them. "We have done well," said those of the underworld. "Where will they go to get flowers now?" they said in their hearts. "Tonight you must give us the flowers; we have already beaten you," it was said to Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque by those of the underworld. "Very well," they said; "tonight we shall play ball," they said, when they made the agreement. And then the young men entered the house of knives, which was the second punishment of those of the underworld. These meant them to be cut by the knives, and thought that they would die at once; but they did not die. And then they spoke to the blades and commanded them: "You shall have all the flesh of the animals," they said to the blades; and they moved no more, but all stayed still. And so they were in the house of knives that night. And then they called all the ants and said, "Cutting ants, thigh ants, come, come all of you; go, all of you, and bring all the flowers we have promised the lords!" "Very well," they said; and all the ants went to fetch the flowers from the garden of Hun-came and Vucub-came. And beforehand the lords had warned those who guarded the flowers of the underworld: "Do not let any flowers be taken, for we have beaten the two young men. And where could the flowers come to them from, since we have beaten them? There is nowhere for them to come from. Keep watch all night!" "Very well," said the guards. And the guards of the garden did not notice; they only kept crying out in vain in the branches of the trees of the garden, and from that came their way of singing and speaking. The one said, "Xparpuec! Xparpuec!" This is what he said, singing. The other said, "Puhuya! Puhuya!" And so the two guards of the garden of Hun-came and Vucub-came are called Puhuya. And they did not notice the ants that were carrying off the flowers they guarded; and the ants came circling around and swaying with the flowers from up in the trees, and with their teeth they gathered those that were beneath the trees. And those who were guarding kept crying out, and did not feel the teeth that were eating their wings and their tails. And so the ants carried off the flowers they cut with their teeth, and very quickly they filled the four gourds with flowers, and these were heaped full when dawn came. And then the messengers who had been sent came and said, "The lord says that those we have beaten are to come at once." "Very well," they said, and they went, carrying the four gourds heaped full of flowers; and they came before the lord, and the lords took the very fragrant flowers. And so those of the underworld were beaten; the young men had sent only ants, and in one night the ants cut the flowers and put them in the gourds. And so all those of the underworld were dismayed, and their faces went pale because of the flowers. And then they called those who guarded the flowers and said to them, "Why have you let our flowers be stolen, which we see here?" "We did not notice, lord," they said, "and look at our tails, how they are." And then they tore their mouths, in payment for letting the flowers be stolen. And so Hun-came and Vucub-came were beaten by Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque, and this was the beginning of their deeds. And from then on the "parpuac" took its mouth in that fashion, torn; so it is torn now. And then they threw the ball and played together; and then they stopped playing ball and agreed and arranged with one another that they would play again in the morning. "Very well," said the young men, when they left the game.
